messages:
mira: following up on the canary/autofallback RFC -- i want to lock down the appeal + rejoin scheduling semantics before we ship the adjudicator PoC. specifically: operator appeals, automated reprobing cadence, and audit trails.
kevin: huge +1. last time we saw variants stuck at 0.2% forever because probe window never ran. need explicit rejoin scheduling.
rahul: proposing two rejoin modes: 1) passive: rely on normal traffic to hit probe buckets; 2) active: scheduled synthetic/mirrored probes that ignore current allocation. active is required for pct < probe_size_pct.
jen: active probes sound fine but privacy/sensitivity for mirrored requests? can't mirror PII in Private mode.
mira: good call. active probes should support three transport options: synthetic (generated payloads), replay (sanitized historical requests), mirror (live but redacted). config controls allowed methods per-deployment.
ops: we should cap active probes to a tenant budget to avoid DDOSing variants. suggest probe_budget_per_hour and probe_rate_limit.
kevin: implementational note: adjudicator should maintain a per-rollout state machine: {RUNNING, SOFT_EVICTED, PENDING_REJOIN, HARD_BLOCKED}. transitions are deterministic. appeals can move from SOFT_EVICTED->PENDING_REJOIN with an operator + optional justification.
rahul: i'll sketch state machine. also add a trust_score in decisions (0..1). low trust actions are logged but not applied unless a global policy allows advisory-only enforcement.
jen: product asks for an "appeal" flow in console where customer can request immediate re-eval (with optional evidence) that triggers active probes. who can approve? operators or tenant owners?
mira: propose roles: tenant-owner can request appeal (creates ticket + audit event, queued), oncall/operator can fast-approve if severity low. for critical routes, operator approval is mandatory.
ops-bot: note: we need alerting for "appeal request denied" and for repeated appeals -> escalation.
mira: sample policy snippet i've been using in PoC: 
```yaml
rollout_id: ab_v92
variant: b
initial_pct: 3
probe_policy:
  probe_size_pct: 0.5
  probe_methods: ["synthetic","replay"]
  probe_budget_per_hour: 10
  max_active_probes_concurrent: 2
rejoin_policy:
  auto_rejoin_after_successes: 3
  rejoin_probe_interval_s: 600
appeal_policy:
  enabled: true
  requester_roles_allowed: ["tenant-owner","se-sre"]
  operator_approval_required_for_critical: true
  audit_log_retention_days: 90
```
kevin: nice. question: how do we prevent probe storms (many appeals for same variant)? add dedupe window + per-tenant cooldown.
rahul: adjudicator will dedupe appeals by hash(route, rollout_id) with a 15m dedupe window. appeals within that window become comments on the original request.
jen: telemetry: want adjudicator.appeals.* metrics + appeal.latency and appeal.outcome. console should show timeline: decision->soft-evict->appeal->probe results->final_decision.
ops: also need immutable audit entries for compliance (who approved, what probe payload used, result). store hashes of payloads, not raw content for privacy.
mira: good. for Private deployments, store audit logs locally only unless tenant opts in to share. provide an export endpoint for auditors.
kevin: routing impact? router subscribe API should accept an action with optional "hold_probe_slot" flag that reserves probe budget for rejoin attempts. prevents other decisions from consuming that budget.
rahul: added: probe_priority integer (higher means schedule earlier). adjudicator maintains a small priority queue and respects max concurrency.
jen: failure modes: 1) probe infra down -> adjudicator should backoff and mark rejoin deferred; 2) probe budget exhausted -> escalate to manual review.
mira: add those to runbook. also add a throttle: when global infra incident (global_circuit_open) we ignore all automated rejoin/probe activities and require manual.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: ab_v92 canary rollout started by @mira at 1766012400, variant b @ 3% traffic. see /deploys/ab_v92
ops: last ask: add a small "why-lost-traffic" API for tenant UI. should return latest decision, reason, confidence, and appeal status. redact any sensitive probe payloads.
mira: agreed. i'll update the RFC with these items: appeal lifecycle, state machine diagram, probe transport options, console wireframe notes, and the audit retention rules. will attach a minimal proto and an initial runbook. follow-up sync tomorrow 11am to review PoC results. :thumbsup:
